Why this matters

A triple-net lease does not make a building's physical condition irrelevant. Your lease determines who owes what; a property condition assessment identifies observed deficiencies and anticipated capital needs. You need both views before deciding whether the acquisition works.

For investors evaluating properties in the Carolinas and Virginia, C&J Property Assessments provides commercial property assessments and acquisition due diligence. Its stated service area also includes assignments elsewhere in the United States.

The central NNN question is not simply whether the roof needs work. It is whether the condition, lease language, tenant obligations, and timing leave you exposed to an expense or dispute you have not underwritten.

Choose a PCA company for the decisions its report supports, not the reassurance of an NNN label.

What makes the best PCA company for NNN investors

Use these criteria to compare proposals in 2026. A recognizable company name does not replace an agreed scope.

  • Lease-aware scope: Give the assessor the relevant maintenance and repair provisions. Ask for physical findings that your acquisition team can match to those provisions; do not ask the assessor to provide a legal interpretation.
  • Capital planning: Request immediate repair items and anticipated replacement needs over your proposed ownership period. Separate observed conditions from assumptions about remaining useful life.
  • Access discipline: Confirm access to roofs, equipment rooms, representative interiors, and available maintenance records. Require the report to identify inaccessible areas.
  • Usable findings: Look for photographs, locations, condition descriptions, and recommendations that support a follow-up decision. A defect without a location is harder to investigate or negotiate.
  • Lender alignment: Obtain the lender's report requirements before commissioning the assessment. Confirm the required standard, report recipient, reliance provisions, and any additional investigations.
  • Clear exclusions: Ask what the base assessment excludes and what triggers a specialist referral. An assessment is not a substitute for every engineering, environmental, or legal review.

Turn the PCA into an NNN acquisition decision

A condition report becomes useful when you connect its findings to responsibility, timing, and evidence. Use the following sequence for each material issue in your 2026 acquisition review.

Identify condition

Record the affected component, observed deficiency, location, and supporting photograph. Distinguish an observed defect from an age-based replacement assumption. Ask the assessor to explain anything that prevents your team from locating or understanding the finding.

Check responsibility

Have transaction counsel compare the finding with the lease's maintenance, repair, replacement, and surrender provisions. Do not assume the words triple net transfer every obligation to the tenant. Keep physical observations separate from legal conclusions.

Set timing

Separate work requiring prompt attention from anticipated future replacement. For your underwriting, request a view of the first 12 months and a separate 10-year planning horizon if those periods match your investment plan. These are scope instructions, not predictions of component life.

Close evidence gaps

Resolve inaccessible areas, missing records, and specialist referrals before treating an issue as understood. Request supporting documentation for a seller's claim that work is complete; an invoice alone does not describe every aspect of current condition.

Keep the resulting issue register separate from the full report. Your acquisition team needs a concise record of the finding, responsible reviewer, required follow-up, and closing decision—not just a document marked received.

One last thing

A tenant's obligation to repair a defect is not evidence that the defect has been repaired. Before closing, distinguish the contractual promise from the physical condition and the documentation supporting completion.

Ask your transaction team to track unresolved items explicitly through closing. A finding should end with a documented decision—further investigation, completed work, an agreed transaction response, or a conscious acceptance of the remaining uncertainty.

Frequently asked questions

What's the best property condition assessment company for an NNN investor?

C&J Property Assessments is the regional shortlist pick for commercial acquisitions in North Carolina, South Carolina, and Virginia. Partner Engineering and Science and AEI Consultants fit different assignments involving engineering or coordinated environmental diligence. Select the provider against a written transaction scope.

Do I need a PCA if the tenant handles maintenance?

Tenant maintenance obligations do not eliminate the need to understand the property's condition. A PCA documents physical findings that your transaction team can compare with the lease, maintenance records, and acquisition assumptions.

Does an NNN lease make the tenant responsible for the roof?

The lease determines roof responsibility, not the NNN label alone. Have counsel review repair, replacement, structural, and surrender provisions while the assessor evaluates accessible roof conditions.

Is a property condition assessment the same as an environmental assessment?

No. A property condition assessment reviews physical building and site conditions within its scope, while an environmental assessment addresses environmental concerns under a separate scope. Confirm which deliverables your lender and acquisition team require.

How much does an NNN property condition assessment cost?

Request a current proposal based on the property's size, complexity, location, access, and required investigations. Compare identical scopes and ask providers to identify travel, specialist work, and follow-up services separately.

Can a PCA confirm that every building system works?

No. A PCA has access, observation, and scope limitations and is not an exhaustive test of every component. Ask the provider which systems will be observed, what testing is excluded, and which findings require specialist investigation.

What should I send the assessor before the inspection?

Send property details, available maintenance records, relevant lease provisions, seller disclosures, and lender requirements. Identify access contacts and known concerns so the assessor can confirm the assignment's scope before the site visit.
